entities.summary:
Louis of Toulouse, also known as Louis of Anjou, was a Neapolitan prince of the Capetian House of Anjou and a Catholic bishop, born in the late 13th century, died on August 26, 1297.

As a member of the royal family, Louis played a significant role in the politics of Western Europe during the Medieval period.

His significance can be understood through the lens of his involvement in the Papal States, where he served as a bishop and participated in the election of Pope Nicholas IV.

The impact of Louis's actions can be seen in the power struggles between the Church and the monarchy, which would shape the course of European history in the centuries to come.

One of the most lasting consequences of Louis's legacy is the rise of the Anjou dynasty, which would go on to play a major role in shaping the fate of France and the Mediterranean region.

This legacy is encapsulated in the quote: "The Anjou dynasty will become the dominant force in the Mediterranean, shaping the course of European history for centuries to come."
